errors.english: so how could that possibility be averted?
errors.why: The Tibetan instructs that the possibility (simultaneous or later arising) is to be refuted as applicable with this same fault; the rhetorical question suggests it cannot be ruled out.

note: A careful rendering of the commentary and the Akṣayamati quotation; only the opening refutation formula is mishandled.
Faithful translation of the argument for the Mahāyāna as buddhavacana, with the opponent's positions correctly attributed.

errors.english: To explain is to describe the specific nature of the transformation and so forth.
errors.why: The commentator identifies the root-text passage that gives the explanation: 'The explanation is "whatever specific transformation" etc.'

fix.find: To explain is to describe the specific nature of the transformation and so forth.
fix.replace: The explanation is the passage beginning "whatever specific transformation."

errors.english: and it is connected to the object of observation
errors.why: dmigs pa here is the verb 'is observed' (upalabhyate) of the root text, with which the phrase is construed, not 'the object of observation'.

errors.english: No matter which word it depends on, the meaning is extracted from that cause.
errors.why: gang gi sgra is 'the word "which" (yad)': in correlation with it, 'from that cause' (tad) is to be supplied.

fix.find: No matter which word it depends on, the meaning is extracted from that cause.
fix.replace: In correlation with the word "which," "from that cause" is to be supplied.

errors.english: depending on which word it relates to
errors.why: Again 'in correlation with the word "which"', the grammatical correlative, not 'whichever word'.

errors.english: One must infer this because a certain result is seen at all times.
errors.why: This sentence belongs to the anticipated objection introduced by 'on te 'bras bu (everything up to ...ཞེས་དོགས་པ་བསུ་བ་ནི), not the author's own assertion.

errors.english: , raising a doubt one or two words at page break
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'it is not so' [refutes] the doubt (the verb is on the next side); 'one or two words at page break' is stray junk and 'raising' misstates the function.

fix.find: , raising a doubt one or two words at page break

note: The commentarial mechanics (correlatives, lemma identification, objection boundaries) are repeatedly misread, and a stray editorial fragment ends the page.

errors.english: For the benefit of others, and
errors.why: With the preceding sbyin, the line says 'illuminating the surpassing excellence of giving'; 'for the benefit of others' is not there.

fix.find: For the benefit of others, and
fix.replace: Making clear the surpassing excellence of giving, and

errors.english: is born into the world of the Sugata One Gone to Bliss
errors.why: prakaṭita-sugatiḥ / bde bar 'gro ba qualifies the jewel of a man (one who has made manifest a happy course), who is born in the world; it is not 'the world of the Sugata'.

errors.english: the virtuous ones find delight in the garden of joy
errors.why: It is the city-dwellers (grong khyer [pa], puravāsinaḥ) who delight in the Nandana-like garden of good deeds; 'good deeds' is the garden, not the agent.

note: The colophon and the opening verses of the Sāketa episode are roughly right but several lines of the kāvya are misconstrued.

errors.english: Even while [note: my mind] was wavering, I did not let go of [note: my resolve].
errors.why: The object is 'that which harms me' (anger, continuing from the previous side): even as it stirred, I did not let it loose; the inserted notes invent a different subject and object.

fix.find: Even while [note: my mind] was wavering, I did not let go of [note: my resolve].
fix.replace: That [which harms me], even as it stirred, I did not let loose.

errors.english: Who is that wrongdoer who, though you were wavering, you did not let go?
errors.why: It is the harmer that was stirring and that the ascetic did not let loose, not the ascetic who was wavering.

fix.find: Who is that wrongdoer who, though you were wavering, you did not let go?
fix.replace: Who is that harmer of yours whom, even as it stirred, you did not let loose?

errors.english: [note: One remains unharmed], like the fading light of the moon at dawn.
errors.why: The verse says ill repute arises for him and his fame fades like moonlight at dawn (contrasting with the waxing moon of the next verse); the bracketed insertion inverts it.

note: The anger verses are mostly sound, but the riddle on which the episode turns (what 'stirred' and was not let loose) is misread through invented notes.

errors.english: Thus it was composed.
errors.why: This is the commentator's abbreviation marker 'apply [the rest] likewise', not a statement about composition.

fix.replace: [The rest] is to be supplied likewise.

note: A good rendering of the abbreviated Sadāprarudita narrative; only one abbreviation formula is misread.

errors.english: [note: referring to a legendary source of fire or lightning, or a specific debate example]
errors.why: brgya byin gyi spyi bo is śakramūrdhan, the anthill, Dharmakīrti's standard example of a thing mistaken for a source of smoke.

fix.find: [note: referring to a legendary source of fire or lightning, or a specific debate example]
fix.replace: [note: Skt. śakramūrdhan, an anthill, Dharmakīrti's standard example]

errors.english: then we state that smoke does not deviate from fire.
errors.why: The Tibetan is a conditional ('if one states that it does not deviate from fire, then how does smoke arise from different auxiliaries?'), the objection the root text voices, not the author's assertion.

errors.english: Now, if one asks: how does fire
errors.why: The side opens with 'and that its existence is just that nature has already been shown', which is not translated.

note: The fire/smoke argument is followed reasonably well, but the śakramūrdhan example is wrongly glossed and one conditional is turned into the author's claim.

errors.english: since it is distinct from the probandum [note: the thesis to be proven] such as the possessor of connection
errors.why: The point is that the probandum is distinct from the conjunct (saṃyogin) reason etc.; the English makes the conjunct an example of the probandum.

note: Sound rendering of the discussion of svabhāva/kārya versus saṃyogin reasons, with one construal slip.

errors.english: uttered various doubts and lamentations about what had truly occurred
errors.why: abhūtārtha-vikalpa-jalpa / yang dag min don: the people broke into talk of imagined, unfounded things, not about what had truly occurred.

fix.find: uttered various doubts and lamentations about what had truly occurred
fix.replace: broke into talk of imagined, unfounded things

errors.english: they have no regard for anything but the wealth they desire
errors.why: The second member of the series says that for one devoted to (others') wishes there is no deference to wealth; it is not a further statement of the greedy man's attachment.

note: The lament over the fallen king is mostly rendered, but the description of the crowd's speech is inverted and one line of the gradatio is misread.

errors.english: "merely the nature" and so on
errors.why: With བ་ལང་ ending the previous side, the lemma is 'merely cowhood' (ba lang nyid tsam), not 'merely the nature'.

errors.english: sets out the enumerated items
errors.why: grangs can is normally the Sāṃkhya; the phrase introduces the Sāṃkhya position, not 'enumerated items'.

note: Accurate tracking of lemmas and objections on universals (cowhood vs animalhood); two lexical slips.
